convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom() for CCI_Woodies indicator and depends on external TradeAlgorithms.mqh library for all trading operations (BuyPositionOpen, SellPositionOpen, BuyPositionClose, SellPositionClose, GlobalVariableDel_, LoadHistory, CIsNewBar). Custom indicator logic is not portable without decompiling CCI_Woodies.

derived_values.name: min_rates_total - minimum bars required before trading
TimeShiftSec - timeframe duration in seconds
derived_values.used_by: UpSignalTime and DnSignalTime calculation for trade signal timestamp

other_exits: Opposite signal closes existing position: buy close when slow CCI crosses above fast CCI; sell close when fast CCI crosses above slow CCI

position_sizing.conditional_logic: MarginMode enum determines sizing: LOT=fixed lot size (MM=0.1), FREEMARGIN=fraction of free margin, BALANCE=fraction of balance, LOSSFREEMARGIN=fraction of free margin minus losses, LOSSBALANCE=fraction of balance minus losses. Default is LOT with MM=0.1.

custom_logic_notes: 1. Invert flag swaps buffer indices (0<->1) so fast becomes slow and vice versa, reversing all signal logic. 2. Signal comparison uses 2-bar lookback: UpIndSeries[1]>DnIndSeries[1] (previous bar fast above slow) AND UpIndSeries[0]<=DnIndSeries[0] (current bar fast at or below slow) was the prior state that triggers buy when crossover confirmed. 3. BuyPosOpen/SellPosOpen/SellPosClose/BuyPosClose are boolean input gates allowing selective enable/disable of each trade direction. 4. Recount mechanism re-reads indicator data on copy failure. 5. CIsNewBar class from TradeAlgorithms.mqh controls new bar detection. SignalBar=0 forces continuous intrabar recalculation. 6. Signal timestamp uses SERIES_LASTBAR_DATE + TimeShiftSec for trade management.
python_conversion_notes: 1. CCI_Woodies is a custom indicator - must be reimplemented in Python. It likely computes two CCI lines (fast period=6, slow period=14) each applied to median price. Standard ta-lib CCI can replicate each line. 2. TradeAlgorithms.mqh provides BuyPositionOpen/SellPositionOpen/BuyPositionClose/SellPositionClose - these handle market execution, SL/TP setting, and position management. Must reimplement as simple market orders with SL/TP in pips. 3. MarginMode LOT is straightforward (fixed lots). Other modes require balance/equity queries from the backtest engine. 4. SL=1000 and TP=2000 are in POINTS not pips - need digit-aware conversion (multiply by 10 for 5-digit brokers). 5. Deviation=10 points for slippage control. 6. The crossover logic reads buffer[1] vs buffer[0] where [1] is the older bar and [0] is the newer bar relative to SignalBar offset - careful with indexing direction in Python.
